claims.text: The starting alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, corresponding nominally to 20 at.% of each element.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
A thin, uniform, adherent CVD alumina coating will significantly improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The CVD alumina coating will improve oxidation resistance without compromising the alloy's inherent mechanical performance.
An adhesion-promoting interlayer can improve coating bonding.
An adhesion-promoting interlayer can accommodate thermal-expansion differences between the alumina coating and the alloy.
CVD at approximately 1000 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressure will form a dense alumina film on HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited alumina coating will be continuous, dense, and well adhered.
The alumina coating acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier on the alloy surface.
The preformed alumina film is a stable, slow-growing barrier during high-temperature exposure.
The alumina film prevents oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature exposure.
Preventing oxygen ingress protects the underlying as-cast microstructure.
Protection of the underlying microstructure preserves the alloy's mechanical properties.
Coated HfNbTaTiZr will show markedly slower oxidation during exposure at 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
Coated HfNbTaTiZr will maintain minimal oxygen penetration after the specified exposure.
After exposure, coated HfNbTaTiZr will retain yield strength and ductility similar to untreated cast alloy at room temperature and 1000 °C over strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant oxygen uptake and associated mechanical degradation at high temperature.
